title: Isao works the AFR-01 with his print beam before he prints the gate
context: Owner, playtesting the live V1 on 2026-09-16: 'before building the gates (nice, works), Isao should use his beam to work on the recycle factory we first see.' The proposal 2026-09-16-isao-tends-the-foundry left the design open: presentational or barrel-driven, how long he stays, and the hard constraint that the gate step is what the tremor waits for, so the first wave pays for every second of the beat.
outcome: Built as a build-programme beat that prints nothing. A step may now carry `over: <structure id>` and a `plot` (half extents in metres): src/fx/base-print.js gives such a step the machine's own footprint as its bed instead of the island it shares, and holds the bed at `metres` from the first frame instead of climbing with the print, so the beam rasters printpath's three patterns across the AFR-01's 16 x 12 m deck at its working height rather than climbing out of the dirt. The step is src/content/base-programme.js `{ id: 'foundry', over: 'foundry', plot: [8, 6], when: { phase: 'rotor-ready' }, seconds: 8, metres: 6 }`, first in the programme; the domain rule (src/domain/build-programme.js) is untouched and every number stays in content. One line, build_foundry: 'AFR-01 is eating our rocket on its own. / Working the cut with the beam. Barrels first, then your gate.' src/td-tab.js needed one line changed (net 0 against the 13,505 budget): the status row reads 'working' for an `over` order and 'printing' for everything else. The foundry's cut is NOT driven by the beat: its own 24 s clock (arc at 2 s, scrap at 10 s, barrel at 15 s) keeps running under him, and the beat is timed in content instead. Tying the beat's end to a barrel was rejected on the timing budget: a window that is guaranteed to contain a barrel is a whole 24 s cycle, and the beat already costs the first wave 14.5 s.
alternatives: Gate the beat on the foundry being mid-cycle (a `cycling` flag into due()) so his work ends as a barrel lands. Rejected: guaranteeing a barrel inside the window needs the full 24 s cycle, three times the timing budget the tremor allows, and a never-satisfied gate would stall the whole programme once the foundry is spent.

Put the beat before `rotor-ready` so it costs the gate nothing. Rejected: there is one drone and one FIFO, so a claimed beat queues the beats' own Rotor order behind it and would delay the Rotor print and the optic hand-over — exactly what the task said not to fight.

Give the beat the landing island as its plot, like every other step. Rejected: the island is 16 x 16 m of ground around the machine, so the raster would have fallen on the dirt beside the AFR-01 rather than on it.
evidence: Two traps found in composition, both silent: src/platform/story-world.js filtered BASE_PROGRAMME to steps whose PIECES the plan holds, so a beat that prints nothing was dropped from the programme entirely; and `standing` (no pending piece) would have marked it done from the first frame. Split into `needs` (pieces plus the machine an `over` beat works) for the filter and `standing` (pieces only, else !grow) for the done set, so the beat is owed on a growing base and already past on a static stage.

test/build-programme.mjs extended: the beat is first, builds nothing, carries no perk, has a cell to fly to (a -1 would stall the programme), its bed sits exactly on the machine's x/z, its height is constant at `metres` at k=0 and k=1, the raster stays inside the plot, and progress()/finish() grow nothing. npm test: 120 test programs passed. npm run check: architecture, line budgets and the frozen module list hold; src/td-tab.js 13,505 lines, unchanged.

Browser --grow through scripts/browser-lock.sh, baseline on d9da03e7 then after 747e85a0, both bare-page stage=1&grow=1, both exit 0 with every step PASS. Seconds from page load. Rotor printed 26.0 -> 25.9; foundry beat begins - -> 25.9; foundry beat ends - -> 38.1; gate print begins 26.0 -> 38.1 (+12.1); gate stands 38.7 -> 53.1 (+14.4); tremor 40.1 -> 54.6 (+14.5); landing pad 48.3 -> 62.3; override 72.9 -> 87.4; first wave cleared 79.4 -> 93.9; Quiver optic 84.8 -> 99.8 (+15.0); settled/handover 99.8 -> 114.7; study 112.4 -> 127.2; expedition 112.6 -> 127.5; solar 134.8 -> 149.3; bays 156.4 -> 171.2; HUGIN 176.3 -> 191.0; radar and assembly 217.9 -> 232.9 (+15.0). The offset is a constant ~14.5 s and does not compound: the whole opening is shifted, not slowed. Of it, 8 s is the beat and ~6.5 s is the flight out to the landing island and back to the gate.

Not browser-verified: the status-row wording (52331bb8) was changed after that run's page had already loaded src/td-tab.js, so the screenshot shows the old 'ISAO printing seed foundry 12%'. The change is a string ternary on a line node --check, npm test and npm run check all pass on, and the line budget is unchanged, but the new 'working seed foundry' text has not been seen in a browser.
The Rotor beat is untouched: the Rotor still prints at 25.9 s (26.0 s baseline) because the beat's `when` is `rotor-ready`, and the Quiver optic hand-over moves only by the same constant shift.

Screenshot artifacts/browser/grow-foundry-beam.png, 5 s into the beat: Isao hovers over the AFR-01 with the beam laid on the machine's deck, the SH02 already swapped for its salvage sections, a barrel on the rack beside it, and the status row reading his line. --grow asserts at that moment that print.step is 'foundry', 0 < k < 1, printed is empty and the gate is not built.

--grow re-run after the change: every step PASS, including grow-foundry-beam, and the final order is ['foundry','gate','landing','stalheart','solar','bays','hugin','radar','assembly'] with all seven perks and the gate's wall count assertion untouched.
